title: F5: the outcome of resolving corrections against one explicit scope context
description: Built by clozn.runs.corrections.resolve_corrections(). A PURE, content-blind computation over discrete scope keys the caller declares (session/client/model/project identities + whether install-wide corrections are included) -- the function signature carries no message content, no prompt text, nothing a relevance/topic matcher could run over. `applied` lists which confirmed+enabled corrections matched by exact scope-key equality, one winner per (type, applicable-scope-set) group; `conflicts` records every case where more than one confirmed+enabled correction of the same type was simultaneously in scope, including the ones that did NOT win -- a conflict is always recorded here even when precedence resolved it automatically, per the standing rule that a resolved-by-precedence outcome must still disclose that a conflict existed and what lost. This document (trimmed to `applied`/`conflicts`) is what clozn.runs.context_receipt.build_context_receipt embeds on the run it was computed for; the untrimmed document is also the shape clozn.runs.corrections.record_applications persists into each affected correction's event ledger, from the SAME call.

conflict.description: One (type) group in which more than one confirmed+enabled correction was simultaneously in scope. `rule` names exactly which deterministic tiebreak decided `winner_id` -- 'precedence' when two different scope kinds disagreed (clozn.runs.corrections.PRECEDENCE_ORDER), 'most_recently_confirmed' when two candidates shared the same scope kind and value, and 'correction_id' as the final, total-order fallback on an exact confirmed_ts tie. Never 'content_similarity' or any relevance-derived rule -- no such rule exists in this codebase.

scope_context.description: The exact, caller-declared scope keys this resolution was computed against -- every key here is either an opaque association key already used elsewhere (session_key/client_key/project_key) or a raw model_sha256 digest. No key is guessed, defaulted from history, or inferred from prompt content.
